svg.text: Apps and Adapters
Iris apps, git-remote-htree, files/sites viewers, shell tools, custom clients
These consumers sit on top of the shared HashTree API surface
HashTree API Surface
Shared put/get/list/mount/traversal operations used by apps and adapters
Publish helpers and tree operations build on the same Store-oriented interface
shared entry point
Optional Publish + Resolve Layer
Mutable Nostr roots and htree:// addresses point at merkle trees
NostrRootResolver maps npub/tree/path and published refs to roots
Direct nhash or CID access can bypass this layer entirely
mutable names only
Content-Addressed Core
HashTree writes deterministic MessagePack trees and chunked blobs
CHK encryption by default with a transport-agnostic Store abstraction
Integrity and deduplication come from the content hash / CID
verified by hash
Mesh Retrieval Layer
BlobRouter routes hash-verified reads across opaque BlobRoute sources
FIPS owns transport addresses; composite routes exclusively select their peers
Bounded adaptive ordering never changes correctness or global absence
transport-generic
Backing Media and Stores
(local, peer-to-peer, server)
Nostr relays for publish/resolve + FIPS discovery, local LMDB, Blossom, S3, memory
hashtree layer stack - apps and adapters on top of the API, optional mutable names above verified content, swappable transport underneath
